newsitem.title: VATICAN: Pope sends support message to Gdansk ship workers.
newsitem.headline: Pope sends support message to Gdansk ship workers.

text.p: Pope John Paul sent a message of solidarity to workers in Poland's Gdansk shipyard on Sunday, saying he was with them in the struggle to save their jobs as he had been in their fight for freedom.

"I want to tell you that, just as I was with you in heart and prayer when you fought for freedom, so I am now with you and your families in this struggle for survival," the Polish Pope said after his regular Sunday angelus address.

"I pray to God that your efforts bear fruit to save this symbol of the historic battles and sacrifices made in defending the dignity of the people and of the nation," he said in Polish. A translation was made available by the Vatican.
Workers from the failed shipyard took to the streets of Gdansk for three days last week, burning tyres and shouting anti-government slogans, in a campaign to save their jobs.
They blamed the government, dominated by ex-communists, for failing to rescue the shipyard -- cradle of the Solidarity trade union which led the overthrow of the old regime in 1989.

The protest has been strongly backed by Poland's former president Lech Walesa, a devout Roman Catholic who is close to the Pope and who founded Solidarity in 1980 when he worked at the yard as an electrician.

The protests in Gdansk erupted after the shipyard's receiver said last Friday he would begin to dismiss the last 3,800 workers of the company, which has operated under bankruptcy regulations since August last year.
